content: Before using homatropine hydrobromide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to belladonna alkaloids (such as atropine), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. After applying this medication, your vision may become temporarily blurred, and your eyes may become more sensitive to light. Protect your eyes in bright light. Infants and small children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug. Avoid allowing this medication to enter a child’s mouth. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you are using this medication on a regular schedule and miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and use your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light. Do not freeze it. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication is used before eye examinations (such as refraction), before and after certain eye surgeries, and to treat specific eye conditions (such as uveitis). It belongs to a class of drugs known as anticholinergics. To apply eye drops, wash your hands first. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before using the drops. Tilt your head back, look upward, and pull down the lower eyelid to create a pouch. Hold the dropper directly over your eye and place one drop into the pouch. Look downward and gently close your eyes for 1-2 minutes. Avoid blinking or rubbing your eye. Do not rinse the dropper. Replace the dropper cap after each use. If you are using another type of eye medication (such as drops or ointments), wait at least 5-10 minutes before applying the other medications. Use this medication regularly to gain the most benefit from it. To help you remember, use it at the same time each day. Common side effects may include burning, stinging, redness of the eye, eye irritation, or temporary blurred vision. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
